subject: general
question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India provides for the promotion of international peace and security?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Article 51**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 51** of the Indian Constitution is part of the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**, which are enshrined in Part IV of the Constitution.
 
• It directs the State to promote **international peace and security**, maintain just and honorable relations between nations, and encourage settlement of international disputes through peaceful means.
 
• The article reflects the guiding principles of India's **foreign policy** and is inspired by the **ideals of the United Nations Charter.**
 
• The inclusion of Article 51 showcases India’s commitment to being a responsible member of the global community and advocating for **peaceful coexistence**.
 
• It also highlights the importance of fostering respect for international law and treaty obligations.
 
• Although the DPSPs are **non-justiciable**, they act as guiding principles for the government while framing policies and laws.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 47**__

 __
 
• Article 47 falls under the **Directive Principles of State Policy** and emphasizes the duty of the State to improve public health and standard of living.
 
• It directs the State to prohibit the consumption of **intoxicating drinks and drugs** that are injurious to health.
 
 
 
• **Article 44**__
 __
 
• Article 44 aims to secure a **Uniform Civil Code (UCC)** across the territory of India.
 
• It is intended to replace personal laws based on the scriptures and customs of each major religious community with a common set governing every citizen.
 
 
 
• **Article 49**__
 
 
• Article 49 relates to the protection of **monuments, places, and objects of national importance.**
 
• It directs the State to safeguard such heritage from spoliation, disfigurement, destruction, removal, and neglect.
